description: Biased grouped top-k router (DeepSeek/GLM/Kimi style): sigmoid (or softmax) scores, keep the best topk_group groups by their top-2 sum of biased scores, pick topk experts inside them, weights are the unbiased scores renormalized times routed_scaling_factor. aiter biased_grouped_topk / sglang grouped_topk.
call: Invoke the live router with the deployment's n_group/topk_group/topk/scoring/renormalize and return (topk_weights, topk_ids) in that order (reorder if the entry returns ids first).

timing.cache: tiny operands; the call is launch-bound in decode. Time it in the deployment graph mode or the number is host dispatch.

negative_controls: select groups by max instead of top-2 sum: different ids on a fraction of rows (multiset_rows rejects)
rank experts on unbiased scores: ids change wherever the bias matters
pitfalls: gating_output is a per-row permutation so no two experts tie; real logits can tie and then any tie order is correct, which multiset_rows on ids alone cannot express. If a task needs tied inputs, add a bound on the selected biased scores instead.
Weights follow their ids: compare them sorted by id (sort_by), never position by position.
In decode this kernel is a few microseconds and runs inside the CUDA graph: an eager UT measures host dispatch, which a graph replay erases.
